page: Amazon Web Services r6a.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 128 virtual CPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor to deliver dedicated CPU allocation.

In benchmark evaluations, the r6a.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% on stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests. Its memory subsystem is highly efficient, achieving top-tier status in read-only small-block memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores. Cryptographic and integer operations are accelerated by hardware flags including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2. Redis SET operations also reach top-tier performance, processing 136.38 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is strong.

A key hardware tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes, and parallel graphics or AI acceleration is limited to CPU-based execution. However, the instance offers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps to mitigate network storage latency. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of DDR4 RAM relative to the 128 vCPUs makes it a highly resource-efficient choice for memory-intensive applications without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated hardware. This profile is optimal for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise database management systems, and memory-bound data processing pipelines.
